title: I Studied NEW Etsy Shops, Here's How I Would Get Sales Fast
key_points: A good goal for starting out on Etsy is 100 sales per month
Product mix should expand to integrate different products achieving different purposes
A shop wanting to target home decor, wedding, or B2B should have 50-60 listings after 6 months
Site merchandising is essential to drive up multi-item orders and increase average order value
Low units and quantities available signals low potential commission to Etsy
Mock-ups for trendy products like ruffle socks with embroidered accents should be pictured in a trendy way
Listings need 18 types of photos for higher conversion rate
Having too many options on a listing hurts conversion rate
Standard everyday 25% off is not recommended
Every listing should have 8 different long-tail keywords
Shops should identify profitable customers and serve them in different areas of their life
Font pairings for 2026 are important to update in shops
Collegiate fonts are not performing as well anymore
The favorite daughter font should replace older all-text design fonts
Bow trends have evolved to more long-tail bows that are more elevated
Wood grain backgrounds should be avoided in product photos
Whitewash backgrounds should be eliminated from shops
Thumbnails should not have text going off the product
Listings should be optimized for mobile since most shoppers come through mobile
Do not create new listings until existing broken unoptimized listings are fixed - they become dead weight
summary:
The video examines 63 Etsy shops that were checked on 6 months prior when sellers said they would make their own growth plans. The presenter establishes benchmarks: 100 sales per month is a good starting goal, and product mix should expand to serve different purposes.

The first shop reviewed has 55 orders but only 8 listings at super low price points in the sourced/handmade category targeting home decor, wedding, or B2B. The presenter states they should have 50-60 listings by now, notes there is no site merchandising (essential for multi-item orders and average order value), the shop is not optimized for Pinterest despite being suitable for it, and low units/quantities signal low revenue potential to Etsy. The pricing strategy is flagged as problematic for shops without momentum.

Subsequent shop reviews reveal common issues: a sock and graduation cap shop with only 104 sales in 2 years needs mock-up redos for trendy products, all SEO updated, 18 types of photos added, and fewer options per listing. A shop with 30 orders over 6 years has only one product type and needs help with design, fit, and font pairings - font duos are specifically not recommended. A digital products shop at 96 sales with Girl Scout items is likely making pennies per hour and missing opportunities to serve profitable customers in different life areas.

Design-specific guidance includes: Kittle designs need post-production work, font pairings for 2026 need updating, the favorite daughter font should replace older text-heavy fonts, collegiate fonts are underperforming, bow trends now favor longer tails with more elevated styling, wood grain and whitewash backgrounds should be avoided, and thumbnails should never have text going off the product. Most shoppers come through mobile, so text-heavy thumbnails with script fonts are difficult to read.

The presenter emphasizes that more listings does not fix problems - fixing existing listings, updating designs, removing poor designs, and updating SEO is the answer. Every listing should have 8 different long-tail keywords, and shops should not compete with themselves using the same SEO across listings. The presenter states clearly that no new listings should be created until all existing unoptimized listings are fixed, as they become dead weight. The video promotes a free weekly workshop-style class for those wanting to take Etsy seriously.
